clue.text: Supply hard-up state with no exposure to outside world

definitions.text: state with no exposure to outside world

indicators.note: read as the adverb from supple, so the letters bend flexibly into a new order

parts.note: the letters of this word, hyphen ignored

explanation.surface: A government bailing out a broke nation that has cut itself off from the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like the verb to provide, but it is the adverb 'in a supple way', bending the next word's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Purdah is the practice of secluding women from public view, hence any condition of isolation from outsiders.

clue.text: Share of profits below expected value

indicators.note: in a down entry, below means the first piece sits under the second

parts.note: par is the expected standard, as in golf
the take is the money earned

explanation.surface: A cut of the earnings coming in under forecast.
explanation.definitionFit: To partake is to take a share or part in something, so it means to share.

clue.text: Sequence obtained from irrational number like 1.618…?

indicators.note: a run of consecutive letters is extracted from the next word

explanation.surface: A maths puzzle about digits drawn from an irrational number like phi.
explanation.walkthrough: 1.618... is the golden ratio, an irrational number, so the surface is literally true.
explanation.definitionFit: The golden ratio is approximately 1.618, so it is an example of the kind of number named, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Recluse beginning to appear agnostic is powerless

indicators.note: lacking power means the letter used for power is taken away
the start of a word is its first letter alone

explanation.surface: A hermit is starting to look like a weakened doubter.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the standard abbreviation for power, removed from the doubter.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic renounces worldly comforts, often living in solitude like a hermit or recluse.

clue.text: Friend of Dorothy embracing man in city

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the dog's name wraps round the man

parts.note: Toto is Dorothy's dog in The Wizard of Oz

explanation.surface: Someone from Oz hugging a man somewhere in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friend of Dorothy' is an old euphemism for a gay man, but here it is meant literally: her little dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Toronto is the largest city in Canada, the capital of Ontario.

clue.text: University dons got upset about popular excursion

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the next piece
to don clothing is to put it on, so the letter is taken into the middle
something upset is knocked over and disordered, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Academics annoyed about a popular trip out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dons' looks like university teachers but is the verb to put on.
explanation.definitionFit: An outing is a short pleasure trip, the same as an excursion.

clue.text: Subtle meaning in obvious jokes

definitions.note: the answer is plural, the definition singular

explanation.surface: Hidden meaning lurking in crude humour.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtones are implied hints or suggestions beyond the literal sense, a subtle connotation.

clue.text: Give evidence providing observer in hearing supports trial

indicators.note: in a down entry a support goes underneath, so this part comes second
within earshot, so the words are taken as spoken

parts.note: providing means if; an eye is an observer; together they say the end of the word

explanation.surface: A witness gives evidence, provided an observer at the hearing backs up the trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' and 'trial' paint a courtroom, but hearing signals a sound-alike and trial is just a test.
explanation.definitionFit: To testify is to make a statement under oath, giving evidence in court.

clue.text: Author right to lift hearts as an aside

parts.note: a parent is the author of a child's existence

indicators.note: in a down entry lifting moves a letter upward; hearts is the card suit, abbreviated H, which moves

explanation.surface: A writer is right to cheer readers up with a side remark.
explanation.walkthrough: The H in the second piece moves up to the front: E-T-H becomes H-E-T.
explanation.definitionFit: A parenthetical remark is inserted as an aside, like words in brackets, interrupting the main sentence.

clue.text: Worry about appearing in newspaper

indicators.note: something appearing in a publication sits inside it, so the short word goes within

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: Anxiety over a story turning up in the press.
explanation.definitionFit: To fret is to be anxious or troubled, a straightforward synonym for the verb worry.

clue.text: Monastery's repeated planning application?

definitions.note: the possessive: Chartreuse is the liqueur made by the monks of the Grande Chartreuse

parts.note: to chart a course is to plan it
use is application, as in putting something to use

explanation.surface: A monastery keeps resubmitting a planning application to the council.
explanation.walkthrough: A chart used once is CHART USE; used again it is CHART RE-USE. 'Planning application' is a British term for asking a council's permission to build.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartreuse is the green or yellow herbal liqueur distilled by Carthusian monks, so it is the monastery's product.

clue.text: Exit is unconventional and quite wrong?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ... of a building
second meaning: ... as slang for weird or avant-garde
third meaning: ..., as in a guess that is far off the mark

explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: the surface reads as a judgment on an exit, but each phrase is a separate sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a door sign, a hippie-era adjective for oddball, and an idiom for an estimate that is badly off.

clue.text: Who published articles in German about scientific topics originally?

definitions.text: Who published articles in German about scientific topics originally?

indicators.note: about here means around, so the outer pieces go round the inner ones

parts.note: ein is the German indefinite article, taken twice for the plural, placed either side

indicators.note: origin means start, so only the opening letter of each word is used

explanation.surface: A quiz question about a famous German-language author of scientific papers.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the most famous physicist published in German, and his surname is the German article twice around two initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein wrote his landmark 1905 physics papers in German for the journal Annalen der Physik.

clue.text: Harry essentially snubbed England after losing almost everything

parts.note: per se is Latin for in itself, essentially
to cut someone is to ignore them pointedly

indicators.note: a word stripped of nearly all its letters keeps only its opening one

explanation.surface: Prince Harry, cold-shouldered, left England having lost nearly everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' reads as the prince, but it is the verb to harass.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to pester or harass relentlessly, and to persecute is to hound someone in the same way.

clue.text: Constant changing of fads and taste

indicators.note: changing alters the arrangement, so the letters of the following words are reordered

parts.note: the letters of the two words, without and

explanation.surface: Fashion and taste keep shifting, and that never changes.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadfast means unwavering and loyal, so it is a synonym for constant in the sense of faithful.

clue.text: Cycle round French city alone

indicators.note: a cycle goes round and round, so the letters rotate, with the end moving to the front

explanation.surface: A solo bike ride around a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: The last two letters of the city move to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Only and alone both mean without any others, as in 'only you' or 'you alone'.

clue.text: Staunch supporter of Kew Gardens?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as a verb, to stop a flow, as of blood
second meaning: the stalk that holds up a plant

explanation.walkthrough: 'Staunch supporter' reads as a loyal fan, but staunch is the verb and the supporter is botanical. Kew Gardens is the Royal Botanic Gardens in London.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem is to check a flow, and a stem is the stalk that holds up a plant's leaves and flowers.

clue.text: Opponents in game involved in sequence played with different sides

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be caught up inside it

parts.note: a scale is a sequence of notes played in order
East and North sit on opposing sides in bridge

explanation.surface: Rivals in a match caught up in a sequence of play from different sides.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North-South partner against East-West, so E and N are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalene triangle has all three sides of different lengths.

clue.text: Part of reign is pale reminder about failing again?

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the run is read backwards
only a portion of the following words is taken, running across their breaks

parts.note: the run starts at the end of reign and stops at the first letter of reminder

explanation.surface: Part of a monarch's reign is a faded reminder of collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading backwards from the R of reminder spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Relapsing is falling back into illness or bad habits, a second failing after recovery, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Fructivorous insect's food

indicators.note: a fruit-eating creature has the fruit inside it

parts.note: a fruit, the kind such an animal eats

explanation.surface: What a fruit-eating bug lives on.
explanation.walkthrough: Fructivorous means fruit-eating, so the insect has swallowed a fruit, here a lime.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliment is a formal word for nourishment or food, related to alimentary.

clue.text: Apprehensive rising star confused over lines

indicators.note: in a down entry something rising reads bottom to top
a lining sits on the inside, so the jumbled word goes within
confusion jumbles things, so the letters come out of order

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming celebrity is anxious, muddled over the script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising star' reads as a newcomer; here it is a star read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Apprehensive and nervous both mean anxious about what may happen.

clue.text: Signs of division in firm lead to insolvency

indicators.note: a lead goes in front, so only the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: Splits within a company lead it into bankruptcy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company, but it is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A solidus is the slash mark used in fractions, as in 3/4, so its plural names division signs.

clue.text: Way of cooking donuts with old jam

indicators.note: to jam is to force something into a tight space, so these letters are pushed inside

parts.note: a torus is a doughnut shape, plural tori
with means and, as in bread with butter

explanation.surface: A recipe for doughnuts filled with old jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Donuts' looks like food but is the geometric shape; 'jam' is not a filling but a verb to push in. T then AND and O then the rest of the shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tandoori describes food cooked in a tandoor, a clay oven from South Asia, so it names a cooking method.

clue.text: Divulge Jack's role

parts.note: the setter is Jack, so Jack is means I am, shortened

explanation.surface: Revealing what character the setter is playing.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by their pen name: Jack's means Jack is, i.e. I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: To impart information is to pass it on or reveal it, the same as divulging.

clue.text: Get rid of undesirable impulse under pressure

indicators.note: in a down entry under means placed below, so this piece comes second

parts.note: an urge is a sudden impulse

explanation.surface: Suppressing an unwanted impulse when stressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undesirable impulse' looks like one phrase, but undesirable belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To purge is to remove unwanted people or things, as in a political purge of undesirables.

clue.text: Eradicate source of nationalism potentially?

indicators.note: something potential is not yet in its final form, so the letters may be put in another order
the source of a word is where it begins, so only its opening letter

explanation.surface: A call to root out the origins of nationalism.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: to deracinate is to uproot people from their native culture, which might well eradicate a source of nationalism.
explanation.definitionFit: Deracinate literally means to pull up by the roots, from French racine meaning root, so it covers both eradicating and uprooting people.

clue.text: Reporter's way to reach source

indicators.note: a reporter speaks the word, so it is taken by how it is said

parts.note: a route is a way, said the same as the answer in British speech

explanation.surface: A journalist finding a route to an informant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source' suggests a journalist's informant, but here it is an origin.
explanation.definitionFit: A root is the origin or basis of something, as in the root of the problem.

clue.text: Writer was aware of inside information

parts.note: to have felt something is to have sensed it
a tip is an insider's hint

explanation.surface: An author knew about some insider knowledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' looks like a person, but it is a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A felt-tip is a pen with a fibre point, an instrument for writing.

clue.text: Trial clears officer in police force

indicators.note: clearing something out removes it, so letters are taken away

parts.note: a time of distress is a trial or ordeal

explanation.surface: A court case acquits a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a court verdict; the trial is a hardship and the officer is removed from its front.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics and engineering, stress is the force acting per unit area on a material.
